ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Context-Encoded Offset Inference for Offline Policies on D4RL Mazes
PROPOSAL: Train an IQL policy on the Maze2d-medium and AntMaze-umaze data, conditioned on a latent vector from a small transformer that reads the last 20 observation-action pairs of the running episode. An auxiliary loss makes the latent predict the injected offset, drawn in training only from constant, step and sinusoidal sequences. At test time the encoder runs at the start and the policy receives its latent. Evaluate on three unseen offset series (random walk, abrupt regime switch, periodic drift) with 5 seeds, reporting normalised return by episode index.
CONTROLS: Compare with plain IQL, IQL with observation noise augmentation, an oracle that receives the true offset, and a variant without the auxiliary loss. Test context lengths of 5, 20 and 50 steps.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Return should recover most of the gap between plain IQL and the oracle soon after an abrupt switch. Failure is likely when offset magnitudes exceed the training range, because the encoder then extrapolates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Offset-Conditioned TD3+BC Policies on Maze and Kitchen Benchmarks
PROPOSAL: Train TD3+BC agents on the Maze2d, AntMaze, Franka Kitchen and Adroit data, pairing each with with a gated recurrent encoder that estimates the offset from the preceding 100 steps. Retrain the encoder from 5 initialisations and tune learning rate, depth and auxiliary loss weight separately for every task, then rerun the whole protocol with a second recurrent cell type and report the gap between the two cell types per baseline. Evaluate on random walk, regime switch, periodic drift, ramp and mixed offset series, logging normalised return by episode index with 5 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare with plain TD3+BC, CQL, observation noise augmentation, an oracle with the true offset, and an encoder-free variant, with learning rate and penalty weight tuned on matching grids in the baselines too.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The recurrent encoder should lift return above plain TD3+BC on most tasks once a new regime begins. It could fail on Kitchen, where long horizons let early offset errors accumulate.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibrating Observation Shifts in the First Steps of an Episode
PROPOSAL: Fit an ensemble of 5 forward dynamics models on the Hopper and Walker2d medium-replay data. At the start of each test episode, estimate the unknown offset by choosing the value that minimises disagreement between predicted and observed next observations over the opening 10 steps, then subtract it from later observations before they reach a TD3+BC policy. Test constant offsets of 5 magnitudes per dimension and a piecewise schedule that jumps between episodes, over 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Baselines are the policy without correction, running mean subtraction of observations, an oracle correction, and a version that estimates the offset from a single step instead of 10, with the Hopper medium-replay and Walker2d medium-replay checkpoints.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Estimation error should fall as the window grows to about 10 steps, and return should approach the oracle. The method may break where the dynamics model is poor in rarely visited regions, which biases the offset estimate.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-Dimension Offset Recovery with Dynamics Ensembles on Locomotion Datasets
PROPOSAL: Fit ensembles of dynamics models on the Hopper, Walker2d and HalfCheetah data of the Gym-MuJoCo suite, refitting the ensemble on resampled subsets. At the start of each test episode, estimate the offset by gradient descent from random restarts over the opening 50 steps, then subtract it from later observations before they reach a TD3+BC policy. Test constant offsets at eight magnitudes per dimension, plus step, ramp and sinusoidal schedules, over seeds and data subsets, logging estimation error after each step.
CONTROLS: Baselines are the uncorrected policy, running mean subtraction, an oracle correction, and estimation windows of 1, 10, 25 and 50 steps, evaluated in each suite.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Estimation error should fall with window length and return should approach the oracle on the 3 suites. Trouble is expected on HalfCheetah, where fast contact dynamics blur the signal that identifies the offset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Forecasting Past Offset Logs to Prepare a Policy Before Each Episode
PROPOSAL: Treat the limited log of past episode offsets as a time series and train a forecaster on synthetic series that mimic abrupt regime changes, seasonal drift and heavy-tailed jumps. Feed the forecast mean and spread to an offset-conditioned CQL policy trained offline on AntMaze-medium-diverse and Adroit pen-human data. Evaluate with log lengths of 0, 8 and 32 past episodes, and with recalibration traces replayed as offsets, using 5 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare forecasters against last-value persistence, a moving average, ARIMA, and N-BEATS. Include an oracle that sees the next offset and a policy that ignores the log.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Learned forecasters should beat persistence only when series have regular structure, and the policy should degrade gracefully when the forecast is wrong. Jump-dominated series are the likely failure, as forecast spread widens and the policy turns timid.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Benchmarking Offset Forecasters and Policies on Families of Series
PROPOSAL: Build families of offset series covering abrupt jumps, seasonal drift, random walks, chaotic maps, bursty noise and recorded recalibration traces, and train forecasters per family from six model classes. Feed the forecast mean and spread to an offset-conditioned CQL agent trained on AntMaze, Adroit and Kitchen data, retraining one agent per family. Evaluate with log lengths of 0, 4, 8, 16 and 32 past episodes, using 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare forecasters against persistence, moving averages, ARIMA, exponential smoothing, N-BEATS and a transformer. Include an oracle that sees the next offset and a policy that ignores the log, with forecast error tabulated within each series family.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Forecast quality should predict return on regular families but not on jump-dominated ones. The comparison could fail if no forecaster beats persistence, leaving the model classes indistinguishable at the evaluated log lengths.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Offset-Randomised Decision Transformers with In-Context Calibration
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a Decision Transformer on Franka Kitchen partial and mixed data after shifting each observation dimension by an offset sampled per trajectory, so a single trajectory shares one offset. The model receives the trajectory prefix and learns to infer the offset implicitly from state-action consistency. Sample training offsets from heavy-tailed and bimodal distributions to avoid fitting a Gaussian shape, and test on non-Markovian series produced by an unobserved regime process with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Controls are a Decision Transformer without offset randomisation, an Implicit Q-Learning policy with history stacking, an oracle with the true offset, and a Gaussian-only randomisation ablation.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: In-context inference should help once the prefix exceeds a few dozen steps, and heavy-tailed sampling should transfer to unseen series. The start of an episode is the weak point, since the prefix carries too little information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sequence Policies Pretrained on Broad Families of Offset Distributions
PROPOSAL: Pretrain Decision Transformers on Kitchen, Adroit, AntMaze and Maze2d data after shifting observation dimensions by per-trajectory offsets from two dozen distribution families, refitting the model at 3 context lengths and four widths. The prefix lets the model infer the offset from state-action consistency. Test on a dozen non-Markovian regime processes with 5 seeds, logging return by step index and logging attention maps.
CONTROLS: Controls are a Decision Transformer without randomisation, IQL with history stacking, an oracle with the true offset, a Gaussian-only ablation, and the same models retrained at each context length, with return tabulated over the unseen processes.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Wider models with longer contexts should give small gains over the single best configuration. The study may fail to teach much if attention maps differ little between processes, so the families add nothing to the result.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latent Shift Encoder Trained by Contrastive Pairs from Clean Trajectories
PROPOSAL: Create positive pairs by taking two windows from one trajectory and shifting both by a shared random offset, and negatives by shifting them by different offsets. A contrastive objective yields an encoder whose embedding captures the offset and ignores state content. Condition an IQL policy on the embedding of the first 8 steps in each test episode. Evaluate on Maze2d-medium and Walker2d medium-expert over 5 seeds under offsets that switch abruptly between episodes.
CONTROLS: Compare against a regression encoder that predicts the offset directly, an unconditioned policy, an oracle, and an encoder trained with only one offset per dataset.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: The contrastive embedding should separate offsets by a gap that grows with offset magnitude, and return should follow. Small offsets relative to state variation are the likely failure, since the two cannot then be told apart.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Contrastive Offset Embeddings with Rich Augmentation Libraries on Locomotion Data
PROPOSAL: Create positive and negative pairs from windows of the Hopper, Walker2d, HalfCheetah, Maze2d and Kitchen datasets, applying shared or distinct offsets together with time warps, dimension dropout and rescaling. Train six encoder architectures under 3 loss functions and condition an IQL policy on the embedding of the first 32 steps of each test episode. Evaluate under offsets that switch between episodes over 5 seeds, training a fresh policy on the setting.
CONTROLS: Compare against regression encoders, an unconditioned policy, an oracle, and encoders trained on one offset per dataset, recording the full set of architecture and loss combinations, together with embedding separation scores for each.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Most architecture and loss combinations should cluster near each other in return, with wider windows helping little. Augmentations that destroy the offset signal would be the main source of failure in this comparison.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Test-Time Normalisation Layers That Re-Anchor Offsets Without Gradient Updates
PROPOSAL: Insert a learned re-anchoring layer before the policy network that subtracts a running estimate of the offset computed from the observation stream with a bounded step size, and train it offline on Maze2d and Hopper data with randomly shifted copies. The layer has fewer than 1000 parameters and needs no retraining at deployment. Evaluate when offsets jump between episodes in patterns the layer never saw, such as square waves of 3 periods and slow ramps, using 5 seeds, measuring how many steps pass before return recovers.
CONTROLS: Compare with batch-statistics adaptation, plain observation normalisation, an oracle re-anchor, and a policy fine-tuned online on the same series.
COST: 520
PREDICTION: Recovery should be fast for step changes and slower for ramps, with no online updates. The layer may lock onto a wrong anchor when the start-of-episode distribution differs from its running statistics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient-Free Re-Anchoring Layers Compared Against Online Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: Insert a learned re-anchoring layer before the policy network, trained offline on Maze2d, Hopper and Walker2d data with shifted copies, using 6 layer designs and 4 step-size schedules. Evaluate on square waves, ramps, chirps and a dozen other patterns, using 5 seeds, and fine-tune a separate policy online in each as a reference.
CONTROLS: Compare with batch-statistics adaptation, plain observation normalisation, an oracle re-anchor, and online fine-tuning with alternative learning rates tried within each pattern. Report recovery speed as the count of steps before return reaches a set fraction of the oracle, with intervals from bootstrap resamples of the seeds.
COST: 520
PREDICTION: Designs should differ little once step size is tuned, with online fine-tuning matching them only after many steps. Patterns that share the same structure would fail to distinguish the designs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling an Offset-Aware Teacher into a History-Free Student Policy
PROPOSAL: Train a teacher IQL policy on Adroit door-cloned and Kitchen complete data that receives the true offset, then distil it in 3 rounds into a student that sees only the current corrupted observation. The student uses a small recurrent core of 2 layers whose state carries inferred offset information, and the distillation loss matches teacher actions on offset-shifted states. This targets deployments where no past offsets can be stored. Evaluate on episodic offsets drawn from step and sinusoidal series with 5 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare the student against the teacher, a behaviour-cloning student without recurrence, plain IQL, and a student trained on clean states only.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: The recurrent student should retain most of the teacher return after a few steps in each episode. Tasks with long idle phases are a risk, since little state motion exists to expose the offset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Teacher-Student Distillation Over Entire Offline Benchmark Collections
PROPOSAL: Train teacher agents with IQL, CQL, TD3+BC and Decision Transformer variants on the Adroit, Kitchen, Maze2d and MuJoCo suites, then distil the teachers into students with 4 recurrent core sizes, covering 3 data fractions. Students see only the current corrupted observation. Evaluate on step, ramp, sinusoidal and random walk offset generators with 5 seeds, repeating the whole distillation pipeline under each fraction and tabulating the spread of student return among the core sizes.
CONTROLS: Compare students against teachers, behaviour-cloning students without recurrence, plain baselines, and students trained on clean states only, in each suite and fraction.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Student return should remain close to the teacher across suites, with little change at smaller data fractions. The pipeline variants may prove hard to tell apart where a single policy class dominates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ensemble Likelihood Tracking of Episode-Wide Offsets with Cautious Acting
PROPOSAL: Maintain a particle belief over the offset during each test episode, weighting candidates by the likelihood of observed transitions under an ensemble of 8 learned dynamics models trained on AntMaze-umaze and Fetch pick-and-place data. The policy acts on belief-weighted actions and falls back to cautious behaviour while the belief is wide. Evaluate on non-Markovian offset series with abrupt switches, over 5 seeds, and report return and belief entropy over the opening steps from each episode.
CONTROLS: Compare with a point-estimate offset, plain CQL, an oracle, and a version that keeps the belief but never acts cautiously.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Entropy should shrink quickly and return should rise above the point estimate when switches are large. When several offsets explain the same short stretch of observations equally well, the method will fail.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Particle Beliefs Over Offsets with Simulation of Candidate Dynamics
PROPOSAL: Maintain a belief with thousands of particles over the offset during each test episode, weighting candidates by the likelihood of observed transitions under learned dynamics ensembles trained on Fetch, Kitchen and Adroit data, refitting the ensemble at 3 model sizes. The policy acts on belief-weighted actions and falls back to cautious behaviour while the belief is wide. Evaluate on two dozen non-Markovian offset series over 5 seeds, measuring return and belief entropy at each step.
CONTROLS: Compare with a point-estimate offset, plain CQL, an oracle, and versions with fewer particles, run on the full set of series.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Entropy should shrink early and return should exceed the point estimate when switches are large, with larger particle sets adding little. The particle set may collapse onto one wrong offset on some series.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pattern Generator and Stress Suite for Test-Time Observation Offsets
PROPOSAL: Build a generator of per-dimension offset series with controllable abruptness, memory length and cross-dimension correlation, and release the specification as a benchmark on Maze2d and Walker2d offline data. Evaluate 3 existing robust offline RL methods and IQL on series that are Gaussian, Markovian, non-Markovian with long memory, and abruptly switching, to show where the usual assumptions fail. Report normalised return as a function of abruptness and memory length, using 5 seeds.
CONTROLS: Controls are the unperturbed environment, a fixed offset equal to the series mean, an oracle with the true offset, and a shuffled series that destroys temporal order.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Methods tuned for noise should lose the most return on long-memory, abruptly switching series. The benchmark may fail to separate methods if the generator parameters have little effect on policy behaviour.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comprehensive Stress Suite for Observation Offsets with Thousands of Generated Series
PROPOSAL: Build a generator of per-dimension offset series with controls for abruptness, memory length, correlation, skew, burst rate and sparsity, and run it on Maze2d, Kitchen and MuJoCo offline data. Evaluate nine existing robust offline RL methods and four baseline learners on thousands of generated series, tuning each method's own hyperparameters per suite, and report normalised return as a function of each control using 5 seeds.
CONTROLS: Controls are the unperturbed environment, a fixed offset equal to the series mean, an oracle with the true offset, and shuffled series, repeated at the settings of the 6 controls.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Return should fall along abruptness and memory length while other controls matter little. Methods may look alike if most generated series fall in easy regions of the parameter space.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-Dimension Offset Structure: Factorised Versus Joint Estimation
PROPOSAL: Compare estimators that treat each state dimension's offset independently with estimators that model correlations among dimensions, on AntMaze-medium, Kitchen and Fetch data. Train a factorised and a joint variational encoder on shifted copies of the data, with offsets in which some joints drift together, as with a shared calibration fault. Test whether joint estimation helps when correlations exist and costs little when they do not, with 5 seeds with a TD3+BC policy conditioned on the estimate.
CONTROLS: Controls are an independent-offsets dataset, a correlated-offsets dataset, a policy without conditioning, an oracle, and a low-rank estimator that sits between the two.
COST: 720
PREDICTION: Joint estimation should win on correlated series by a clear gap and tie on independent ones. If the data lack enough dimensions to reveal correlations in the first steps in an episode, the advantage will vanish.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Estimator Zoo for Offset Structure: Factorised, Joint, Low-Rank and Hierarchical Variants
PROPOSAL: Compare seven estimator families, from factorised to joint, low-rank, hierarchical and mixture-of-experts, on the Kitchen, Fetch and MuJoCo offline data. Train each estimator at 3 capacities on shifted copies with six correlation structures, and condition a TD3+BC policy on its estimate. Test each estimator under each correlation structure with 5 seeds, and fit separate controllers in the estimator, dataset and structure.
CONTROLS: Controls are independent and correlated offset sets, a policy without conditioning, an oracle, and a rank sweep from 1 to the full dimension within each task, with estimation error tabulated for every correlation structure.
COST: 720
PREDICTION: Joint estimators should win on correlated structures and tie on independent ones, with hierarchical models gaining little. The families may converge to near-identical estimates on most datasets.
